plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Increase QQQI to 15% to favor income and stability.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, aiming for lower drawdowns. However, this also limits upside potential.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Reduce SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
Buy CRM at 4% to add a high-scoring quality tech name.
Trim QQQI to 10% to rebalance the income allocation.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for approximately 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing high-quality tech. Expect moderate drawdowns with balanced growth potential.

plan: Increase SOXL to 6% and SPAL to 6% to lean into leveraged ETFs.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
Buy CRM at 6%, MSFT at 5%, and NVDA at 5% to concentrate in high-scoring tech setups.
This strategy uses leverage and concentration for aggressive growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring tech. This approach carries substantially higher drawdown risk and is subject to daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Increase QQQI to 30% to prioritize income and monthly distributions.
Trim SPY to 20% to rebalance the broad index exposure.
Sell CRWD and SMH to zero to reduce high-beta single name exposure.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income from covered-call ETFs. While aiming for steady distributions, NAV can still fall in a selloff, and distributions are variable, not guaranteed.
